taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-a-item

parts.text:
You are a hydrogeologist preparing site notes for a borehole drilling team.

Station T-02 (survey area T). Interpreted VES layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 31374.7 | 20.07 | 20.07
2 | 7559.9 | 12.79 | 32.86
3 | 3573.3 | 1.62 | 34.48
4 | 313.2 | 38.90 | 73.38
5 | 53.6 | 0.41 | 73.79
6 | 22.8 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this sounding curve as K-type.

Write the site note using exactly this template:

Station: <station name>
Curve type: <VES curve type>
Aquifer depth: <depth range in m>
Recommendation: <one or two sentences for the drilling team>

Reference note: Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station: T-02
Curve type: Q (recomputed from resistivity sequence — all four triplets give Q: 31374.7>7559.9>3573.3, 7559.9>3573.3>313.2, 3573.3>313.2>53.6, 313.2>53.6>22.8; this differs from the K-type label on file and should be re-checked against the raw sounding data before finalizing)
Aquifer depth: 73.79 m to base of investigated section (Layer 6, 22.8 ohm-m, resistivity remains low with no lower boundary defined)
Recommendation: Plan drilling to at least 74–80 m to fully penetrate the low-resistivity (22.8 ohm-m) basal layer identified as the primary aquifer target, and install casing/seal through the overlying 313.2 ohm-m and 53.6 ohm-m layers (34.5–73.8 m) to prevent cross-contamination; flag the curve-type discrepancy for the interpretation team before finalizing the pump-test design.
